 Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J. 
1.
Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I, for the State, apprised the Court that he has received the instructions, therefore, the instant anticipatory bail application may be finally disposed off.

2. Heard Sri Yawar Mukhtar, learned counsel for the applicant and Dr. S.B.Maurya, learned AGA-I,
for the State.
3.

The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on anticipatory bail in Special Session Trial No.330 of 2023 arising out of Case Crime No.1236 of 2019, under Section 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, Police Station Cantt.
District Varanasi during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2019 against the applicant and four others and as per allegation applicant was Accountant on contractual basis in Uttar Pradesh Poorva Sainik kalyan Nigam Limited, Varanasi and he along with others misappropriated the public fund of more than Rs. Three Lacs but entire allegations levelled against the applicant are totally false.

sentences.text: 5. He further submits that after lodgement of the FIR of the present case applicant was arrested in the present matter for offences punishable under Sections 120B, 471, 468, 467, 406, 420, 419 and 409 IPC but Coordinate Bench of this Court on 2.12.2020 was pleased to enlarge him on regular bail and the copy of the bail order has been annexed at page 65 of the paper book.

6. He next submits that after investigation even charge sheet was filed against the applicant for the offences in which he was enlarged on bail by this Court but thereafter investigation of the case was transferred to Economic Offences Wing (EOW) and during further investigation conducted by EOW offence under Section 13(2) PCAct has been added and thereafter applicant applied for anticipatory bail for offence under Section 13(2) P.C.Act before the court concerned then his anticipatory bail application has been dismissed 7.
He further submits that even EOW has already submitted supplementary charge sheet without arrest of the applicant.
8. He further submits that there is no allegation that applicant did not cooperate with the further investigation.

9. He further submits that as charge sheet has been filed for offence u/s 13(2) PC Act after further investigation, therefore, after submission of charge sheet there is no need of custodial interrogation of the applicant.

10. He further submits that applicant is having apprehension that if he will appear before the court concerned then he will be sent to jail, therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case it is not proper to send him behind the bar.

sentences.text: He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history to his credit.
12. Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

14. FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2019 against the applicant and four others and as per allegation applicant was Accountant on contractual basis and he along with others misappropriated public fund of Rs. Three Lacs Twenty Eight Thousand Seven Hundred Fifty but it reflects that when during investigation conducted by the Police he was arrested for offences under Sections 120B, 471, 468, 467, 406, 420. 419 and 409 IPC then this Court on 2.12.2020 enlarged him on bail and thereafter charge sheet has been filed
but after submission of the charge sheet it appears that investigation was transferred to EOW and during further investigation conducted by EOW offence under Section 13(2) PC Act has been added.

15. Record further suggests that EOW during further investigation did not arrest the applicant though applicant cooperated with the investigation and without his arrest supplementary charge sheet has been filed against the applicant for offence under Section 13(2) PC Act.
16. Considering the above facts, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant that now there is no need to send the applicant behind the bar.
17. Further, considering general practice adopted by the court concerned now-a-days, apprehension of arrest raised by applicant cannot be ruled out.
18. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history to his credit.

19. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail.
20. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.
